changelog: Replaced C1 to emphasize checking the suffix-alone contradiction risk and to instruct preferring leftward cuts onto non-assertive/function words so prefixes stay inert — addresses both findings.
Inserted a worked example (append) showing a mistaken post-assertive cut: 'He announced the plan would fail.' so scorers learn to move cuts left onto function words.
Replace C1 to make high-contradiction risk explicit and actionable (addresses underweighting of contra in findings).
Paraphrase C2–C7 to shorten and keep their judgments while reducing prompt length (size reduction).
Replace C8 to emphasize preferring non-assertive prefixes (move cut left) and to warn against cutting after content heads (addresses habit of cutting after heads).
Delete examples E2, E4, E6, E10, E11, E12, E13, E14, E15, E16, E17 to meet size budget and keep a focused set of representative examples that illustrate the failures named in the critique.
Replace E1 with measured example en_us_888 to teach moving cuts left onto non-assertive prefixes (addresses finding that scorer cuts after content heads).

Replace E2 with measured example en_us_741 to show danger of splitting numeric/measure phrases and the need to treat suffixes that can overturn factual claims as unsafe (addresses underweighted contra risk).
Replace E3 with measured example en_us_105 to illustrate high-contradiction suffixes (relative clauses like 'from which ...' that can negate or change preceding assertion).

Replace E4 with measured example en_us_924 to emphasize that suffixes supplying essential instrumentation or scope (e.g. 'that can be called ... without charge') raise contra and should be ranked unsafe.
